turn_text: Anything in the works in Congress? Are you watching anything come down the pipeline in terms of money for either dairy or agriculture that will benefit Wisconsin producers?

Oh, absolutely. So at the same time we're looking at the funding on the appropriation side, the Senate Ag Committee is working on the 2023 Farm Bill. We know that there will be a lot of support to continue programs that work well and are doing showing a strong record. There'll be things that will be tweaked and there'll probably be some new initiatives. But I do want to note one thing outside of the Farm Bill that may happen knock on wood this week is we've reached a bipartisan agreement on school nutrition waivers. What do I mean by that? I mean that during the pandemic, we waived some of the red tape and rules around the school nutrition programs. It allowed families that were struggling to be able to get food throughout the summer when school is out of session. And we know that the pandemic-related program is due to expire at the end of this month. And we hope to be able to renew it for the summer at minimum and hopefully beyond then. And you're confident in that bill? Well I'm confident that we have a bipartisan agreement worked out. What I am not confident about is whether every member will be in support of it but I think ultimately we will have that path and that will mean great things for students and their parents access to fresh nutritious food over the summer months when they're not getting breakfast or lunch in schools. And we know what a difference that those waivers made during the pandemic. And we're not quite out of the pandemic yet. So I think there's a good argument that these should last for a couple months to come.
